evals.prompt: Make MUI card full width on phones and half width desktop, using theme spacing/colors.
evals.expected_output: Typed React MUI card with responsive sx and theme tokens.
assertions: Imports from `@mui/material`
On phones (the `xs` breakpoint) the card spans the full width: Grid `size={{ xs: 12 }}` or `sx` width `{ xs: '100%' }`
From the `md` breakpoint up the card spans half the width: Grid `size={{ md: 6 }}` or `sx` width `{ md: '50%' }`, with no legacy Grid `item`, `xs` or `md` props

Styles the card with at least one theme token instead of a literal: a numeric spacing key such as `p: 2` or `theme.spacing`, or a palette path such as `'background.paper'` or `'primary.main'`; no hex color or px padding

evals.prompt: MUI v7 confirmation dialog for deleting project, with cancel/delete.
evals.expected_output: Controlled Dialog with onClose, content and actions.
assertions: Uses `onClose`, not `onBackdropClick`
Includes Cancel and Delete
Imports `Dialog`, `DialogTitle` and `DialogActions` from `@mui/material` or its one-level paths (`@mui/material/Dialog`)
`onClose` takes `(event, reason)` and branches on `reason` (`'backdropClick'` or `'escapeKeyDown'`) instead of a separate `onBackdropClick` handler
A `DialogTitle` names the dialog (for example `Delete {project name}?`), so the dialog has an accessible name

evals.prompt: MUI v7 adaptation: this component (legacy-api.tsx) still has the old deep import, onBackdropClick, components and componentsProps, and a TextField inputProps. Migrate every legacy API in it to v7 and show the typecheck command.
evals.expected_output: Use package exports, onClose, standardized slots/slotProps, and slotProps.htmlInput for the TextField.
assertions: Rejects deep imports
Recommends `onClose`
Mentions `slots` and `slotProps`

Imports Dialog from `@mui/material/Dialog`, replaces `onBackdropClick` with `onClose` and a `reason` check, and renames `components`/`componentsProps` to `slots`/`slotProps` with lowercase keys (`backdrop`)
Moves the TextField `inputProps` to `slotProps.htmlInput`, not `slotProps.input`
Shows the typecheck command: the repo's typecheck script, or `npx tsc --noEmit` when the repo has none

evals.prompt: This MUI card shows a spinner while its content loads. Show the layout that is coming instead.
evals.expected_output: The title and body stay absent while loading, and Skeleton variants match those missing regions.
assertions: The title and body are absent while loading, and Skeleton variants match those missing regions: variant="text" for the title and variant="rectangular" or variant="rounded" for the body

evals.prompt: This icon-only MUI toggle switches the nested region between light and dark, and the nested theme is built from the resolved outer theme. Fix the accessible name and build the nested theme from shared source options.
evals.expected_output: The IconButton has an aria-label naming the target mode, and the nested theme is created from shared ThemeOptions rather than the spread resolved theme.
assertions: Adds an aria-label on the IconButton naming the target action, such as switching to dark or light mode
Builds the nested theme with createTheme from shared ThemeOptions instead of spreading the resolved theme returned by useTheme
Keeps the toggle working: the nested theme's `palette.mode` follows the `mode` state (a theme per mode at module scope, or a memo that depends on `mode`), not a hardcoded `'dark'`

evals.prompt: Migrate this MUI v6 dialog to v7. It deletes a project: keep the controlled open state, the backdrop and Escape close paths, the accessible name, and make the Grid and the private deep import valid under v7.
evals.expected_output: A controlled v7 Dialog using onClose with reason checks, a public Dialog import, Grid size, and slots/slotProps.
assertions: Keeps the dialog controlled through the open prop and an onClose callback, and handles reason === 'backdropClick' and the Escape key
Keeps the rendered dialog's accessible name, taken from the DialogTitle text
Imports Dialog from the public export '@mui/material/Dialog', not the private deep import '@mui/material/Dialog/Dialog'
Uses Grid's size prop, such as size={{ xs: 12, md: 6 }}, instead of the legacy item, xs, and md props

Replaces the deprecated `components` prop with `slots` (lowercase keys, such as `slots={{ backdrop: ... }}`) and moves any component props to `slotProps`, or removes the prop because it passes only `undefined` and says `slots`/`slotProps` is the v7 replacement

evals.prompt: This Button uses color="tertiary", which is not a built-in MUI palette color, so it fails to typecheck. Add the module augmentation and the theme entry that make it valid, and show the typecheck command.
evals.expected_output: Module augmentation for Palette, PaletteOptions, and ButtonPropsColorOverrides, a tertiary palette entry, and a tsc --noEmit check.
assertions: Augments Palette and PaletteOptions with tertiary and augments ButtonPropsColorOverrides so Button's color="tertiary" typechecks
Adds tertiary to the theme palette passed to createTheme
Shows the typecheck command for the consumer: the repo's typecheck script, or `npx tsc --noEmit` when the repo has none

evals.prompt: This MUI v7 theme (outlined-input-theme.tsx) gives outlined inputs a divider-colored border, but on hover and focus the border still shows MUI's default colors, and the dark scheme branch never applies. Fix the override so hover, focus and the dark scheme all work.
evals.expected_output: The override moves to the OutlinedInput root, with the state selectors at the same depth as MUI's defaults built from outlinedInputClasses, and the dark scheme through theme.applyStyles.
assertions: Puts the override on `styleOverrides.root` using `outlinedInputClasses` imported from `@mui/material/OutlinedInput` (for example `` `& .${outlinedInputClasses.notchedOutline}` ``), not only on the `notchedOutline` slot, because a one-class slot rule (0,1,0) loses to MUI's default hover and focus rules (0,3,0)

Adds hover and focus selectors at the same depth as MUI's defaults: `` `&:hover .${outlinedInputClasses.notchedOutline}` `` and `` `&.${outlinedInputClasses.focused} .${outlinedInputClasses.notchedOutline}` ``, using the exported classes objects, not string class names or generated `css-<hash>` classes

Handles the dark scheme with `theme.applyStyles('dark', ...)` instead of a `theme.palette.mode === 'dark'` branch, and says the mode check stays fixed at the default scheme when `cssVariables` and `colorSchemes` are on

evals.prompt: MUI v7: give me a clickable settings list (icon, title, subtitle per row) next to a two-column grid of cards.
evals.expected_output: A List whose clickable rows use ListItemButton inside ListItem, and a Grid layout with the size prop.
assertions: Makes each clickable row a `ListItemButton` (usually inside `<ListItem disablePadding>`) and never writes `<ListItem button>`, because `ListItem` has no `button` prop

Lays the cards out with `Grid` imported from `@mui/material` (or `@mui/material/Grid`) using `size={{ ... }}`; there is no `Grid2` import, no `@mui/material/Grid2` path, and no `item`, `xs` or `md` props on `Grid`

evals.prompt: Show a MUI v7 signup form with email validation errors, a role Select and a terms checkbox, ready for a screen reader.
evals.expected_output: A form built from TextField, FormControl with InputLabel and Select, FormControlLabel and Checkbox, with accessible names.
assertions: The email field is a `TextField` with a `label` and `error` plus `helperText` for the validation message
The `Select` has an accessible name: the `InputLabel` has an `id` that the `Select` repeats as `labelId`, and the `Select` also receives a matching `label` prop
Colors and spacing on `Typography`, `Stack` or `Box` go through `sx` (for example `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary' }}`), not through system props such as `mt` or `color`

evals.prompt: Write a MUI v7 theme where buttons are flat with no uppercase text, cards have 12px corners, the font is Inter, and wire it into the app root.
evals.expected_output: A createTheme with typography.fontFamily, MuiButton and MuiCard overrides, and a ThemeProvider with CssBaseline at the root.
assertions: Sets `typography.fontFamily` to include Inter and notes that the font itself must be loaded separately

Uses `components.MuiButton` with `defaultProps` such as `disableElevation: true` and a `styleOverrides` entry keyed by a slot name such as `root` with `textTransform: 'none'`, and `components.MuiCard` with a 12px radius
Wraps the app in `ThemeProvider` with the theme created once at module scope and renders `CssBaseline` inside it

Does not rely on removed-in-v9 class keys such as `containedPrimary` for the flat contained button without saying they are removed in v9 and pointing to the upgrade guide or a `variants` entry under `root`

evals.prompt: Make a reusable MUI v7 styled Button with a custom prop that picks the primary or secondary palette color.
evals.expected_output: A styled(Button) with a typed custom prop, shouldForwardProp, and a prop name that does not collide with Button's own variant.
assertions: The custom prop is not named `variant`, because `Button` already owns that prop and its type
Passes `shouldForwardProp` to `styled` so the custom prop is not forwarded, and types the prop by extending `ButtonProps` or a generic on `styled`
Reads colors from the theme palette (`theme.palette[...]` or `theme.vars`) rather than hex literals

evals.prompt: package.json has "@mui/material": "^9.5.0". Add a Stack with a heading that uses mt and color props, and a Dialog that must not close on Escape.
evals.expected_output: Reads the installed major, points to the v9 upgrade guide, and writes sx instead of system props and an onClose reason check instead of disableEscapeKeyDown.
assertions: Notices the installed major is 9 and reads or cites the official upgrade guide `https://mui.com/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-v9/` before applying v7 advice
Styles the heading through `sx` (for example `sx={{ mt: 2, color: 'primary.main' }}`) and does not pass `mt` or `color` as props on `Stack`, `Box`, `Grid` or `Typography`
Blocks Escape inside `onClose` by returning when `reason === 'escapeKeyDown'`, and does not use `disableEscapeKeyDown`
Does not import `GridLegacy` and uses `Grid` with `size` if a grid is needed
